interpretation: The interaction between Glucose and SkinThickness does not provide a statistically significant predictive advantage over Logistic Regression. The likelihood ratio test (p=0.6942) and bootstrap confidence interval for the interaction coefficient (-0.00088 to 0.00061) indicate no meaningful effect. The primary ROC-AUC and secondary Accuracy metrics were not specified in the results but the model comparison shows no improvement from adding this interaction.
observations: Likelihood ratio test chi2=0.1546 with p=0.69416
Wald test p-value=0.6921 for interaction coefficient
limitations: No explicit ROC-AUC or Accuracy values reported for model comparisons
Bootstrap confidence interval includes zero, indicating no significant effect
Lack of comparison with other models (Random Forest, XGBoost) in the results
The interaction effect is negligible in magnitude and not statistically significant
next_hypothesis: Testing whether adding BMI as a feature interaction with Glucose provides a statistically significant predictive advantage over Logistic Regression in the diabetes prediction model.
